name: Philip Burroughs
role: Seneca County farmer whose home hosted early preaching
dateNote: Section 30, from September 1830, sends John Whitmer to preach at his home.
importance: Section 30 tells John Whitmer that his labor will be at Philip Burroughs’s home and the region around it. Church meetings were held in his home near Fayette that autumn. There is no record that he joined the Church himself.
connections: His wife, Anna Parker, was baptized. The revelation calls him John Whitmer’s “brother”, probably as a fellow believer or friend rather than a relative.

sources.title: Philip Burroughs, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP: born 1794, New Jersey; War of 1812 veteran; married Anna Parker 1815 in Fayette; lived in Seneca Falls by 1830; wife baptized, no record of his own membership; died in Portage, New York (date shown as a fragment, 25 July 1865). The reading of “brother” is my inference.
